question: What made Golgi's 1873 silver stain able to show a single neuron whole?
answer: Its unreliability. His black reaction darkens only a few cells in every hundred, seemingly at random, but each one entirely; stain every cell and the slice would be solid black. Why it picks those cells is still unknown. Cajal used it to show neurons are separate cells; Golgi denied it in his 1906 Nobel lecture.
move: Show everything at once and nothing can be seen.
source: Shepherd, Foundations of the Neuron Doctrine, 1991
reference: Shepherd, Foundations of the Neuron Doctrine, Oxford University Press, 1991
